finalText:
The migration is complete.

**Changed files (12)**

- `packages/accounts/src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`
- `packages/accounts/src/repo/session.js`
- `packages/accounts/src/service/teamService.js`
- `packages/analytics/src/repo/cohort.js`
- `packages/billing/src/repo/refund.js`
- `packages/billing/src/service/couponService.js`
- `packages/catalog/src/admin/variantAdmin.js`
- `packages/catalog/src/repo/supplier.js`
- `packages/orders/src/repo/shipment.js`
- `packages/orders/src/service/returnService.js`
- `packages/support/src/admin/macroAdmin.js`
- `packages/support/src/repo/sla.js`

Each file had three call sites. The rewrite is mechanical: `db.query(sql, params)` becomes `db.execute({ sql, params })`. The SQL strings and the parameter arrays are unchanged, so behaviour is the same. All 78 JavaScript files pass `node --check`.

**Not changed**

- `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (lines 9 and 13) still calls `db.query`. The file header says that the vendored copy is replaced on every upgrade, and that local edits are lost. I left it alone. To remove the last two call sites, you must upgrade `legacy-orm`, or wrap the adapter in your own module.
- `cache.query(...)` in several repo files is a different API on the cache handle. It is not part of this migration.

One note: `db.execute` accepts a `timeoutMs` option that `db.query` could not carry. I did not add it anywhere. If specific call sites need a timeout, tell me which ones.
